title: Trump’s ‘Morally Binding’ AI ‘Accord,’ the Rise of AI Agents, and Extremists on the Ballot
byline: Brian Barrett, Zoë Schiffer, Leah Feiger
excerpt: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we discuss the voluntary AI safety agreement tech executives signed, AI agents for normies, and extremist candidates running for office in the US midterms.
content_html:
This week on Uncanny Valley, Brian Barrett, Zoë Schiffer, and Leah Feiger discuss the “morally binding” AI accord that tech executives signed following a meeting with Donald Trump. They’ve agreed that AI labs will regulate themselves—should work out great. Plus, the team digs into OpenAI’s Developer Day, where CEO Sam Altman introduced AI agents for normies, otherwise known as Dots; how AI agents are coming to workplaces near you; and a quick rundown of the most extremist candidates running for office.

  • Trump’s AI Safety ‘Accord’ Is a Fancy Pinky Swear
  • These Extremists Are Running for Election in November
  • A Pentagon Influencer Called Liberal Women a ‘Pestilence’ Who Will End Western Civilization
  • The White House is Starting to Panic Over the Midterms
  • I Think I Found an AI Agent Worth the Risk
  • AI Agents Are About to Flood the Workforce
  • I Built AI Clones of My Coworkers. Things Got Weird
  • Why No One Wants to Date Tech Bros

So you're sort of getting it from both sides from the government.

佐伊·希弗：是的。 And we have Lina Khan writing an op-ed in The New York Times today saying they actually can be tried under existing laws. We don't necessarily need to make new laws, with the big caveat that Congress would have to act.

Zoë Schiffer: I personally think Republicans are going to do great in the midterms, but you can cut that because I am not reporting on politics and that's just my vibe check.

Leah Feiger: I'm changing my mind constantly.
